newsitem.title: GERMANY: German shares weaker, but hold around record highs.
newsitem.headline: German shares weaker, but hold around record highs.

text.p: German shares opened bourse dealings a shade weaker on Tuesday as they responded to a modest loss on Wall Street overnight and some weakening of the dollar against the mark.
Traders said they expected the market to trade quietly in a narrow range as it consolidates at new record high levels.
"We should stay plus or minus twenty points around these levels today," said one dealer.
"Business is quiet. I don't expect any spectacular developments today," said another.
The DAX index of 30 leading blue chip shares traded 5.86 points or 0.22 percent lower at 2,696.79 early in the session.
"We can slide a little bit or move sideways over the next few days and then take another run up beyond 2,700," said one trader.

Sportsware manufacturer adidas jumped 1.80 marks to 143.80 marks in bourse trade. The stock earlier reached a year-high of 145 marks on the back of news that it would be an official sponsor for the 1998 soccer World Cup.

Airline Deutsche Lufthansa also moved against the trend, gaining over one percent to 223.50 marks after it said a co-operative alliance with Scandinavian airline SAS would improve its net earnings by 100 million marks in 1997.
